title: NCLT Kolkata: Homebuyer Insolvency Threshold Is Measured by Actual Bookings, Not a Developer's Proposed Unit Count
case_name: Evanie Eco Nest Home Buyers Association v. Evanie Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.
card_summary: A homebuyers' association sought to admit a Section 7 insolvency petition against a stalled project's developer near Baruipur. The developer argued the petitioners fell short of the IBC's minimum allottee count, citing a higher proposed-unit figure. NCLT Kolkata rejected that, holding the threshold is measured by actual bookings on the filing date, and admitted the petition.
card_tip: If a developer resists a homebuyers' Section 7 petition by citing a higher unit count, check whether that count reflects actual sold units; the threshold counts real bookings on the filing date, not planned project size.
verification_notes: Chosen for the IBC & Insolvency practice area with a direct Kolkata angle, since the NCLT Kolkata Bench decided it and the project itself is located at Baruipur in South 24 Parganas, West Bengal; stalled housing projects and homebuyer insolvency petitions are a recurring dispute category in the Kolkata property market. Case name, C.P.(IB) No. 285/KB/2021, the 9 October 2026 decision date, and the core holding (threshold measured by actual bookings/allotments, not proposed units) are confirmed across two independent reports (LiveLaw Biz and Taxscan), with a third (TaxGuru) corroborating the outcome. The exact buyer count and default amount are reported inconsistently across sources (one citing 59 buyers and roughly Rs 3.43 crore, another referencing a 540-unit baseline dispute) and are therefore not stated as fixed figures in this card. Not previously covered on the site, which has general homebuyer-as-financial-creditor guides but not this specific threshold-calculation ruling.
